source.title: Texas Notifiable Conditions - 2026
source.publisher: Texas Department of State Health Services

general_reporting_rule: Report all confirmed and suspected cases. Unless a condition is marked with an asterisk, report to the local or regional health department. Also report outbreaks, exotic diseases, unusual disease groupings of public-health concern, and select agents by the most expeditious means.
workday_calculation_note: Work-day deadlines skip weekends. The PDF does not define a holiday calendar, so holidays are not excluded by the deadline calculator.

footnotes.1: Use the specific Texas HIV/STD reporting rules for reporting requirements and destination.
footnotes.2: Reporting forms and investigation guidance are available from Texas DSHS. Call the listed 24/7 number for immediately reportable conditions.
footnotes.3: The listed laboratory isolates or specimens must be submitted to the Texas DSHS Laboratory Services Section or another designated public health laboratory; see the PDF for the organism list and submission details.
footnotes.4: Secure select-agent isolates and specimens under applicable regulations and immediately consult public health about testing or sequencing.
footnotes.5: Arboviral infections include California serogroup, chikungunya, dengue, EEE, Oropouche, SLE, WEE, West Nile, and Zika viruses, among others.
footnotes.6: Blood collection centers have additional reporting duties for reactive West Nile, Zika, Babesia, and Chagas donor tests to the DSHS Zoonosis Control Branch; the PDF specifies contacts and required donor information.
footnotes.7: Use Texas DSHS asbestosis reporting instructions.
footnotes.8: Report suspected botulism immediately by phone at 888-963-7111.
footnotes.9: Follow Texas Cancer Registry reporting rules and requirements; the condition table does not specify a general deadline.
footnotes.10: Use the Texas DSHS acute occupational pesticide reporting instructions.
footnotes.11: CRE includes Escherichia coli or Klebsiella species resistant to at least one carbapenem or producing a carbapenemase.
footnotes.12: The PDF includes sporadic, genetic/familial, iatrogenic, and other named prion diseases; see it for the full surveillance scope.
footnotes.13: Use the local health department’s Varicella Reporting Form instead of an Epi-1 or Epi-2 morbidity report.
footnotes.14: Contaminated sharps injury reporting applies to governmental entities, not private facilities (Texas Administrative Code §96.201).
footnotes.15: Report controlled substance overdoses through https://odreport.dshs.texas.gov/.
footnotes.16: Novel severe acute respiratory coronaviruses include MERS and SARS; call immediately for these or another novel coronavirus. COVID-19 is no longer a Texas notifiable condition as of March 1, 2024.
footnotes.17: Follow the specific Texas injury reporting rules for reporting and destination.
footnotes.18: Laboratories must report syphilis test results within 3 work days of the testing outcome, in addition to the condition-level reporting timelines shown in the table.
footnotes.19: Texas DSHS Hansen’s disease reporting forms are available online.
footnotes.20: Reportable TB disease includes suspected disease pending final lab results, positive nucleic acid amplification tests, confirmed disease, and the listed M. tuberculosis complex species.
footnotes.21: TB infection requires a positive approved IGRA or skin test, a normal chest radiograph, and no TB symptoms; report skin test results in millimeters.
footnotes.22: Report any person suspected of having HIV, including HIV-exposed infants.
footnotes.23: Use Texas DSHS lead reporting instructions for the required call/fax route.
footnotes.24: Also report any outbreak, exotic disease, or unusual disease grouping of public-health concern by the most expeditious means; this includes select agents. See the PDF for mpox requirements.
